Managed worker routing

Opt-in code-enforced worker routes with fresh capacity checks, durable provider affinity and explicit context budgets.

About 8 min read · 4 sections

On this page
01 Configuration 02 Context and cache behavior 03 Rollout 04 Limits

Managed aliases opt into provider selection in Gateway code. Ordinary aliases, explicit model choices, native reviewer routes and existing worker models retain their exact bindings. The client still owns task scope, permissions, delegation, tool execution and context compaction.

new managed worker
  -> enforce caller context byte budget
  -> local model with fresh health, when suitable
  -> suitable subscription with fresh quota above its reserve
  -> explicitly enabled DeepSeek V4 Flash only when every configured
     subscription candidate has a confirmed blocker
  -> persist the chosen provider/account/model binding before inference

later requests -> the same binding, including across Gateway restarts

By default, busy queues and unknown or stale quota never authorize paid escalation. Pro, GLM and other paid models are excluded from managed candidate chains. An explicit ordinary model request remains an explicit selection; these rules do not turn an unrelated fixed alias into an automatic route. Independent review remains an explicit separate model choice.

Configuration

Add managedRouting.routes to the existing Gateway configuration. Candidate aliases must already exist under providers, and their declared context windows must support the managed route's advertised window. For example:

{
  "managedRouting": {
    "routes": {
      "managed/routine": {
        "purpose": "routine",
        "candidates": ["qwen/qwen3.8-flash-next", "claude-primary/claude-sonnet-5-5", "codex/gpt-6.1-sol", "or-deepseek"],
        "contextWindow": 32768,
        "maxContextBytes": 262144,
        "minRemainingPercent": 2,
        "allowPaid": true
      }
    }
  }
}

Default candidate order is local models, subscriptions, then paid Flash. A strong route starts with subscriptions and cannot contain local candidates. Paid routing defaults off. Missing subscription quota is unknown capacity, even when an availability row otherwise says available. A cold managed request starts the existing collectors and waits at most 2.5 seconds; it refuses if no eligible route is known after that wait. No provider call occurs on a refusal.

A routine policy can explicitly set preferPaidFlash: true together with allowPaid: true to select local models, then paid DeepSeek V4 Flash, then subscriptions. This opts into per-token Flash spending even while subscriptions have quota; it is not a claim that paid tokens cost less than prepaid allowance. Flash still needs fresh positive balance and availability, compatible reasoning and context, and the existing Flash-only model restriction. Strong/review policies cannot select this preference. Omitted settings retain the previous admission rule and policy fingerprints. Use a fresh alias to preserve existing worker pins.

The HTTP request uses the managed alias as its model and supplies a stable thread-id or session-id. Managed aliases are internal worker policies, omitted from /v1/models and the normal desktop model picker. /v1/model-catalog retains them with visibility: "hide" so configured worker roles and existing managed chats remain routable. An explicit hidden-model listing can inspect them. The catalog advertises common reasoning capabilities, a text-only input surface and the configured context window. Managed aliases advertise Gateway's V2 client collaboration contract independently of an upstream's model-discovery metadata; fixed model rows keep their existing metadata. This version does not change account setup or the native app's connection-management UI.

Context and cache behavior

autoCompactTokenLimit optionally advertises an explicit SDK compaction threshold. It must fit inside 90% of the configured context window. Omitted values preserve existing policy fingerprints and catalog behavior.

Coding and test roles need headroom beyond the client's stable instructions and tool definitions. The current 131,072-token profiles allow a 1 MiB serialized request and compact at 104,857 tokens. Their role files also set model_context_window and model_auto_compact_token_limit explicitly. This keeps a newly added alias bounded even when an already-loaded SDK lacks that alias in its frozen model catalog and would otherwise use generic defaults. The real-SDK fixture exercises both known and missing catalog rows at 60K reported input tokens, requiring task progress without compaction churn.

The verified SDK also honors paired overrides for the named qwen/qwen3.8-flash-next worker model. That fixed model keeps its normal route; context overrides do not opt it into managed selection. Earlier SDK builds only honored these fields for managed/*, so checking a named role's file alone did not establish its effective window. Run the named-worker fixture documented in releasing before activating a changed fixed-role limit.

Use fresh internal policy aliases for widened profiles. Existing pins and their old limits remain intact; old workers are not moved, restarted or silently assigned a different account. A larger window is a ceiling, not a request to fill it, and does not promise maximum context at maximum concurrency.

An optional candidateReasoningEfforts map explicitly selects a provider-specific effort for that internal policy. Each key must name one of its candidates and the value must be an effort that candidate supports. This is an opt-in profile, not an automatic increase for all models: an implementation policy can map only Qwen to xhigh while its subscription and Flash candidates retain the caller's medium. The map applies to managed requests only; fixed model requests bypass it. The response includes X-Gateway-Managed-Reasoning-Effort when a map entry was applied. Use a new policy alias for this change so existing pinned workers keep their original policy and reasoning behavior.

Start a fresh worker with a bounded task, selected evidence, allowed files, acceptance checks and a compact handoff. A client role may select a managed alias for future workers; this does not rewrite roles or restart an existing worker. The byte budget includes the serialized caller request, including instructions, tool definitions, metadata and history. It is an exact payload limit, not an exact tokenizer or a promise about the provider's hidden framing.

Over-budget requests fail before inference with the existing context_length_exceeded code, so clients can enter their normal compaction recovery. Gateway never silently drops, summarizes or changes caller messages, tool results, instructions or permissions. The client must compact its own context or start a fresh bounded worker.

A request marked compaction has a separate recovery allowance of four times maxContextBytes, capped at 4 MiB. It requires an existing durable worker pin and uses that same provider with the same capacity checks. It cannot establish a new binding or bypass an unavailable provider. Requests beyond the recovery allowance still fail before inference; subsequent ordinary turns retain the original byte limit. This makes room for the client to summarize accumulated history without increasing its normal worker context budget.

The persisted pin avoids model/account churn and preserves the opportunity to reuse the same provider's prefix cache. For a local Chat Completions model, configure the existing sessionAffinity: true option so the worker's identifier also reaches its upstream router. A pin does not by itself guarantee a cache hit; cache availability and eviction remain upstream behavior.

An unavailable pinned provider produces a refusal. It is never silently replayed onto another provider after a partial stream, tool call or missing usage. The caller may retry that provider, or start a new worker ID with a plaintext handoff. A paid pin under the default policy also refuses when its prerequisite subscription blockers no longer hold. Explicitly preferred Flash pins keep their binding while their own paid capacity remains eligible. Provider-specific opaque state cannot start an unbound managed worker. A changed policy or provider binding requires a fresh worker.

Rollout

Release the reviewed Gateway change before enabling managed aliases. On each target machine, require gateway rollout --verify --json to report ready and the authenticated /health response to advertise managed-worker-routing-v1. Then add the explicit route configuration and verify /v1/model-catalog retains the hidden worker aliases while /v1/models offers only named models. Do not add another daemon or force-restart active chats to enable this feature.

For future client workers, select managed/routine in the implementation/test role's model setting. Preserve that role's instructions, sandbox, tool access and permissions. Existing workers keep their loaded model; a new worker or engine picks up the managed alias and its bounded context metadata. Keep main chat models and independent reviewer roles explicit. Selecting a fixed alias continues to bypass managed selection deliberately.

Pins bind the configured provider, credential source and model. They do not inspect login or API-key file contents to audit an account replacement in place; an operator replacing an account must start fresh managed workers. Pins contain only configured route identities and fingerprints under the owner-only stateDirectory/managed-route-pins directory. Raw prompts, tool arguments and thread IDs are not persisted there. Unsafe or corrupted pins fail closed; they never trigger a fresh provider selection. There is no automatic pin eviction that could silently move an old conversation after restart.

Limits

The offline real-SDK check for hidden worker roles is node scripts/e2e-subagent-sidebar.mjs --package VERIFIED_PACKAGE --code CHECKOUT --root TASK_DIRECTORY --v2 --role-fork --managed. It requires a configured role to spawn a hidden managed worker, execute a real fixture command, retain its model across resume and follow-up, and expose the pinned model in Activity. All inference uses local mocks and private homes. Repeat with --managed-stale-catalog to verify explicit role limits when the worker alias is missing from the executor's frozen catalog. Add --managed-compact to cross the configured threshold once and require real compaction followed by successful tool execution and continuation.

This is provider admission before inference, not an agent scheduler or automatic semantic task classifier. Candidate suitability comes from the explicit managed alias and its configured capabilities. It does not retry another model after inference starts, invent task summaries, or override a provider refusal.

OpenRouter's balance check is a fresh capacity fact, not a durable financial reservation. Wieldr's separate OpenAI credit guard continues to own its 2% dollar reserve and charge ledger. Managed worker routing does not extend that financial guarantee to other API callers or providers.
